topics.title: Section A: The Qur'an and Sunnah

outcomes.text: Describe the Prophet's early years and first proclamation up to 622 CE.
Explain his challenges to Meccan beliefs.
Explain the Hijrah and its significance.
Describe his administration and leadership roles: religious, political and military.
Explain his morals, manners and character as an example to Muslims.

subtopics.title: Qur'an set texts: character and society

outcomes.text: Explain Qur'an 3:144 on the Prophet and how it relates to the Sunnah.
Explain Qur'an 4:12 on inheritance and its application today.
Explain Qur'an 5:89-90 on intoxicants.
Explain Qur'an 10:99-100 on freedom of belief.
Explain Qur'an 13:3-4 on signs in creation.
Explain Qur'an 17:31-34 on orphans.
Explain Qur'an 17:35 on fairness.
Explain Qur'an 25:68-70 on punishment.
Explain Qur'an 31:14-15 on parents.
Explain Qur'an 31:17-19 on prayer and arrogance.
Discuss how the Prophet is a perfect example, using these sources.
Explain Hadith 1 on sincerity.
Explain Hadith 18 on repentance.
Explain Hadith 27 on perseverance.
Explain Hadith 54 on truthfulness.
Explain Hadith 73 on piety.

subtopics.title: Hadith set texts: faith and relationships

outcomes.text: Explain Hadith 75 on firm belief.
Explain Hadith 85 on steadfastness.
Explain Hadith 199 on hypocrites.
Explain Hadith 309 on neighbours.
Explain Hadith 316 on parents.
Show how these Hadith apply to Muslim lives today and how the Prophet is a perfect example.

topics.title: Section B: Islamic beliefs, practices and ceremonies

outcomes.text: Explain belief in a single Creator God (tawhid).
Explain the role of prophets as human messengers (risalah).
Explain angels as deliverers of books and recorders of actions (malaikah).
Explain revealed books as guidance for humankind (wahy).
Explain the Day of Judgement and the afterlife (akhirah).
Explain life as a test within fate and predestination (qadar), and how beliefs are shown through actions such as the Five Pillars.
Describe the rituals of purification for prayer, Hajj preparation, birth and death.
Explain purification of the mind through right intention (niyyah) and of the heart through the shahadah.
Explain fasting in Ramadan (sawm) as physical and spiritual renewal.
Explain almsgiving (zakat) as purification of wealth.
Describe daily and occasional prayer, including the five daily prayers, Eid prayers and special occasions.
Explain worship (ibadah) and developing God-consciousness (taqwa).
Explain the family's role in building faith and marriage (nikah) as commitment.
Describe diverse devotions, such as Ashura and personal supplication (dua).
Explain support for the poor through zakat, voluntary donations and charity.
Explain how devotion, including Hajj, creates equality in the ummah.
Explain inclusion in the Eid festivals and the value of sacrifice shared in family and community.
Explain the link between intentions, actions and belief in judgement and the afterlife.

units.title: Paper 2 Islamic law (shariah) and its application

topics.title: Section A: Schools of Islamic jurisprudence (fiqh)

outcomes.text: Compare opinions on purification (wudu) before prayer.
Explain timings and conditions for daily prayers, combining prayers, and fajr, asr and maghrib timings.
Explain the conditions for Friday prayers (Jumuah).
Compare opinions on marriage to relatives and to those of other faiths.
Explain freedom of choice of marital partners and conditions for divorce (talaq).
Explain questions of inheritance, especially shares for female relatives.
Explain principles of trade and business transactions.
Explain handling debt, usury and interest (riba), and mortgages.
Explain employment in different local contexts according to Islamic principles.
Study the opinions of two schools of fiqh on worship, family life and finance.
Choose one Sunni madhab (Hanafi, Shafii, Maliki or Hanbali) plus another Sunni, a Shii school or a reformist or Salafi perspective.
Compare interpretations between the two schools and across the content areas.
Explain the primary sources: Qur'an and Sunnah, progressive revelation, and strong and weak Hadith.
Explain secondary sources: consensus (ijma), analogy (qiyas) and reasoning (aql), and differing views on their use.
Explain references to the people of Medina, local custom (urf), the companions and their followers.

topics.title: Section B: Diversity of schools of thought

outcomes.text: Compare literal and metaphorical readings of anthropomorphic references to God and the effect on the Qur'an's authority.
Explain the statement of faith and Ali's position for Shii Muslims.
Compare opinions on celebrating the Prophet's birthday.
Discuss spiritual relationship with God in mystical poetry and the controversy over Mansur al-Hallaj.
Explain the Sunni Caliph and Sunni Imams appointed by merit.
Explain the Shii Imam in Muhammad's family line and his error-free interpretation.
Explain the Sufi master (murshid), the order (tariqa) and dhikr.
Discuss how far individuals may interpret teachings (ijtihad) for the modern world.
Explain interpretations of the Mahdi and the return of the twelfth Imam for Shii Muslims.
Explain the Sufi path through spiritual stations towards union with God.
Explain the Mutazilah and rationalism applied to justice in the afterlife.
Discuss free will versus predestination (qadar) and the possibility of adjusting the Divine plan.
Compare Sunni beliefs with the Shii party of Ali and leadership from the Prophet's family.
Compare the Mutazilah with the views of al-Ashari.
Describe the mystical approach of Sufism with examples of orders.
Compare modern Salafi literal reinterpretation with modernist reformist application of principles.
Compare the schools on tawhid, religious leaders and the afterlife.

topics.title: Section A: The Umayyads and Abbasids

outcomes.text: Describe the leadership of the Umayyad caliphs.
Explain their religious, educational and trade policies.
Critically assess their rule against the Qur'an and Sunnah.
Explain the change in art and culture from pre-Islamic Arabia to the Umayyads.
Describe the development of the minaret and architecture reflecting Islamic beliefs.
Study one Umayyad achievement: the Grand Mosque of Damascus, Masjid al-Aqsa, or the Grand Mosque and Palace of Cordoba.
Explain the legacy of interfaith relations in Muslim Spain.
Describe the leadership of the Abbasid caliphs.
Explain their religious, educational and trade policies.
Critically assess their rule against the Qur'an and Sunnah.
Explain the importance of openness to the translation movement.
Compare Abbasid science, observation and evidence with the modern scientific approach.
Study one Golden Age achievement: Al-Khwarizmi's algebra, Ibn Sina's Canon of Medicine, or Ibn al-Haytham's optics.
Explain the legacy of safeguarding knowledge and progress in science.
Compare Umayyad and Abbasid leadership and policies.
Compare how far each caliphate followed the Qur'an and Sunnah.
Analyse their contribution to a studied area such as education or religious facilities.
Evaluate the influence of their legacies for Muslims today.
Explain that God sends knowledge through revelation and signs in nature studied through philosophy (falsafah).
Compare Islamic philosophy with the writings of the ancient Greeks.
Compare the different ways of deriving beliefs: revelation, observation of creation, philosophical reasoning and mystical meditation.
Evaluate ways Muslims explain their beliefs to others (dawah) today.
Compare two significant writings chosen from Ibn Tufayl, Al-Ghazali, Ibn Khaldun, Rabia al-Adawiyya, Al-Biruni or a candidate's choice.
Explain each work's contribution to learning and its perspective on Islamic beliefs.
Explain how art and architecture express belief: geometric patterns, domes and the Garden of Paradise.
Explain how Islamic art differs from pre-Islamic Arabia: removal of idols and calligraphy of the 99 names.
Compare two mosques from a prescribed list and how they reflect Islamic beliefs.
Discuss how far artistic expression and cultural diversity should be embraced.
Discuss whether environmental stewardship and preserving architecture is an obligation.
Compare how a belief such as tawhid is expressed through philosophy and through architecture.

units.title: Paper 4 Islam in the modern world

subtopics.title: Women in Islam: position and rights

outcomes.text: Analyse the position of Muslim women in modern society, equality with men and the challenges they face.
Compare Muslim opinions on women's role and rights in shariah.
Explain women's rights in marriage and their roles in family life.
Discuss issues of religion and culture: dress, greeting, careers, prejudice and discrimination.

subtopics.title: Women in Islam: Qur'an, history and role models

outcomes.text: Evaluate how far women's position today follows the Qur'an and Sunnah.
Assess how far women's rights improved with Islam and how far these are applied now.
Explain the influence of Khadija, Aisha and Fatima as role models.
Study the contributions of two Muslim women from history, such as Lubna of Cordoba, Razia Sultana or Noor Jahan.
Study one influential contemporary Muslim woman and evaluate her contribution.

subtopics.title: Islam and pluralism: minorities and rights

outcomes.text: Analyse the position of minorities in Muslim societies and Muslims as minorities in mixed societies.
Compare opinions on the rights of people of other faiths in shariah.
Explain the extent of rights to freedom of thought, belief and expression.
Discuss religion and culture issues: prayer at work, festival leave and building mosques.

subtopics.title: Pluralism: Medina, history and case studies

outcomes.text: Evaluate how far treatment of other faiths follows the early Medina community, the Sunnah and the Qur'an.
Assess how far non-Muslim rights improved with Islam and are applied today.
Explain the influence of Caliph Umar and the Dhimmi contract.
Compare historical approaches: Akbar and Aurangzeb, or Muslim rule in Spain.
Study two countries or communities, such as Mauritius, France or Malaysia, for pluralism and inter-faith relations.
Analyse Muslim leadership in majority countries and in minority communities.
Compare opinions on the qualities needed to be a leader.
Explain Muslims' human rights and responsibilities to leaders.
Discuss just rule, provision for the less fortunate and responses to corruption and oppression.
Evaluate how far leadership today follows the Qur'an and the Prophet's leadership in Medina.
Assess how leadership improved from the pre-Islamic Shaykh.
Discuss support for democracy and consultation, with examples from the Four Rightly-Guided Caliphs.
Study two Muslim leaders who shaped modern practice, such as Abduh, Maududi, al-Banna, Syed Ahmad Khan or Iqbal.
Study one contemporary Muslim leader and evaluate them against Islamic principles of leadership.
Compare content across 4.1, 4.2 and 4.3, such as a woman studied with a leader studied.
